newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says not right time for German envoy's return.
newsitem.headline: Iran says not right time for German envoy's return.

text.p: Iran wants a warm relationship with the European Union but Germany must wait before its ambassador can return to Tehran, President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said on Sunday.

Iran last month temporarily banned Bonn's ambassador Horst Beschmann over a German court verdict implicating the Islamic republic's top leadership in the assassination of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant in 1992.

Asked at a news conference if the ban was still in place, Rafsanjani said: "Yes. It was mentioned by the leader of the revolution (Ayatollah Ali Khamenei) that the ambassador of Germany could not return for a while, and I believe that Germany should wait a bit more.
"Their attitude has not been appropriate...It was bitter for us that the demands of Israel and America were being fulfilled by Germany, a country friendly to us."
But he added: "God willing, this restriction should be annulled. Patience, however, is constructive for humans."
Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said last week Germany would have to "rectify" its mistake in implicating Iran in the four Mykonos killings.

The Berlin judge had said a secret "special operations committee" whose members included Iran's supreme religious leader, president, intelligence minister and head of foreign policy ordered the shootings.

Velayati said a statement by the German federal prosecutor that an investigation into Iran's leaders would not be pursued was unsufficient. German prosecutors issued arrest warrants for three Iranian intelligence officers.
Rafsanjani, due to step down in August following Friday's election of moderate cleric Mohammad Khatami as his successor, told reporters Iran wanted normal relations with the European Union.
"We are interested in a natural, warm and healthy relationship" he said.
EU ambassadors left Iran when they were called home for consultations after the German verdict and the 15-member bloc suspended its policy of "critical dialogue" with Tehran.
Rafsanjani said Iran had been thinking prior to the latest tension with the EU that it would benefit all Asian countries to extend Iranian cooperation.

"Priority should be given to working with Asian countries and this irrational move of the European Union has strengthened us in the previous thoughts that we had," he said in the two-hour news conference.
